view: Wide ground-level archaeological study Babylon low weathered baked-brick wall foundations and earthen mounds, a shallow excavated corridor foreground, flat alluvial plain and sparse date palms. No complete blue Ishtar Gate, no Hanging Gardens, no intact ziggurat or modern reconstructed palace.

eras.title: Walls of earth and brick
eras.caption: Babylon's remains spread across a broad plain beside the Euphrates. Excavated brick walls and low mounds preserve parts of a city repeatedly rebuilt by its rulers; much of its former scale has to be read from the ground rather than a skyline.

evidence.basis: Interpretive study of surviving archaeological remains, including excavated or conserved fabric. The era begins at the dataset abandonment date to associate the study with the ruin phase; it does not date the illustrated state of excavation or assert that habitation ended permanently in that year.
